statement: Tlaloc's iconography is traceable to Teotihuacan (Classic period, pre-900 CE), centuries before the Mexica arrived in the Valley of Mexico — one of the clearest cases in this batch of a deity the Mexica inherited from an earlier regional tradition rather than originated. Tlaloc co-occupied the Templo Mayor's twin-shrine summit alongside the Mexica-specific Huitzilopochtli, a documented statement of the Mexica state deliberately pairing an ancient, regionally shared agricultural deity with its own newer war/imperial patron.

sources.citation: General art-historical/archaeological consensus on Tlaloc's Teotihuacan-era iconographic origins, corroborated across Templo Mayor excavation reporting on the twin-shrine summit arrangement.
